system_description.narrative_title: Global bond selloff and rising yields amid hawkish central-bank pivot
system_description.narrative_summary: A synchronized global surge in government bond yields is reshaping markets as central banks shift toward tighter policy and commodity-driven inflation fears (notably oil and energy) rekindle rate-hike expectations. The situation is an open system: cross-border capital flows, central-bank communication/actions (Fed, ECB, BOJ), fiscal financing needs, and geopolitical shocks continuously interact with investor positioning and market interventions, producing reinforcing and balancing feedbacks across yields, currencies and asset allocation. Market actors' responses (from sovereign treasuries to hedge funds and interventionists) alter the system state in real time, creating contagion risks for borrowing costs and financial stability.
system_description.scope: Global government bond markets and yield curves; central-bank policy decisions and forward guidance (Fed, ECB, BOJ, RBNZ); inflation drivers (energy prices, supply shocks), investor flows and positioning (funds, sovereigns, hedge funds), currency moves and market interventions; fiscal financing pressures for sovereigns and associated feedback into markets.
system_description.super_system: Global financial and macroeconomic system (capital markets, international trade, monetary and fiscal policy interaction)
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and commodity markets (oil, gas)
Geopolitical risk and regional conflicts (Middle East tensions)
Sovereign fiscal policy and public debt markets
Equity and corporate credit markets / financial stability

variables.name: Policy short-term rate level
variables.description: The prevailing short-term policy interest rate that anchors short-term funding conditions across the system.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: The market-implied consensus about the future path and timing of short-term policy interest rate changes.

variables.name: Long-term government yield level
variables.description: The prevailing yield level on long-dated sovereign debt instruments that reflects discounting of future cash flows.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The component of long-term yields that compensates investors for interest-rate risk and other long-horizon uncertainties.

variables.name: Yield curve slope
variables.description: The difference between long-term and short-term yields indicating the term structure shape and expectations about growth and rates.

variables.name: Realized inflation rate
variables.description: The measured rate of change in consumer prices over a recent period as experienced in the economy.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The anticipated future inflation trajectory as held by households, firms, and market participants.

variables.name: Commodity price level
variables.description: The current price level of key commodities (notably energy) that drives cost-push inflation pressures.

variables.name: Fiscal financing need
variables.description: The aggregate government borrowing requirement over a fiscal horizon that determines sovereign issuance pressure.

variables.name: Sovereign credit spread level
variables.description: The average risk premium demanded over risk-free benchmarks to hold sovereign debt, reflecting credit and liquidity concerns.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flows
variables.description: Net financial flows across borders into and out of fixed-income and related markets over time.

variables.name: Market liquidity
variables.description: The ease with which bonds and related assets can be transacted without large price impact, measured by depth and bid-ask dynamics.

variables.name: Investor positioning
variables.description: The aggregate directional exposures of major investor groups, including duration, leverage, and net long/short stances.

variables.name: Systemic leverage
variables.description: The overall leverage in the financial system, including margining and balance-sheet risk amplification potential.

variables.name: Market intervention intensity
variables.description: The frequency and scale of deliberate market operations or asset transactions by policy actors to influence prices and yields.

catalysts.title: Fed September policy decision
catalysts.description: An FOMC decision in September (possible hike) will directly shift short-term policy and market pricing across yields.
catalysts.rationale: Markets see Warsh endorsing a rate hike in September; Warsh hints Fed may raise if inflation doesn't fall.

catalysts.title: ECB September meeting (likely hike)
catalysts.description: Eurozone inflation back above 3% raises odds of an ECB rate increase at the upcoming meeting, pressuring sovereign yields.
catalysts.rationale: Euro zone inflation above 3% cements ECB rate-hike bets; top ECB official urges readiness to lift rates further.

catalysts.title: BOJ September rate decision
catalysts.description: BOJ signalling a September hike could end big stimulus, shifting global flows and raising Japanese yields.
catalysts.rationale: BOJ chief signals chance of September rate hike; Japan faces day of policy reckoning after stimulus calls.

catalysts.title: Continued oil and energy price surge
catalysts.description: Ongoing energy-price strength (Middle East/gas) sustains cost-push inflation, lifting expectations and long-term yields.
catalysts.rationale: Energy price surge and oil rises jolt bond markets; Middle East turmoil rekindles inflation worries.

catalysts.title: Treasury / investor yield‑capping actions
catalysts.description: Treasury or large investors may undertake operations or big purchases to cap long-term yields, altering market dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Coverage cites Bessent/Treasury interventions and talk of 'Operation Twist 2.0' to cap long‑term yields.

catalysts.title: Sustained hawkish central‑bank communications
catalysts.description: Ongoing hawkish messaging (Warsh, ECB, BOJ) will keep rate-path expectations and yields elevated even absent immediate hikes.
catalysts.rationale: Warsh's Jackson Hole hawkish stance and ECB/BOJ signals keep markets pricing tighter policy and higher yields.

catalysts.title: Rising fiscal financing pressure
catalysts.description: Higher yields push up governments' borrowing costs, increasing fiscal financing needs and widening sovereign spreads.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note higher yields add tens of billions to G7 debt costs and strain UK/France bond markets.

catalysts.title: Trading‑firm market‑structure strain
catalysts.description: Increased activity by trading firms and curbed bank lending could reduce bond-market depth and amplify price moves.
catalysts.rationale: JPMorgan curbed lending to Jane Street as trading firm muscled into bond market, flagging liquidity and structure risks.
